macro_context.coverage_period: 2025 calendar year (synchronous-area-wide aFRR + mFRR + FCR procurement)
macro_context.interpretation: Strongest macro anchor for Baltic balancing-market spend size. KKME revenue projections sized at single-MW level scale linearly against this number (€74M ÷ ~752 MW eff demand → ≈ €98k/MW/yr Baltic-aggregated balancing spend, before TSO margin and product-level allocation).
macro_context.afrr_methodology_note: KKME afrr_up_avg / afrr_down_avg = rolling 7-day mean of BTD price_procured_reserves (Lithuania, capacity-reservation €/MW/h). Not directly comparable to Clean Horizon's June 2025 "Baltic S1 2025 Price Forecasts" (€77 up / €340 down, aggregate-Baltic, Apr–mid-Jun 2025 launch window) — that window predates summer-2025 market deepening (~1.5× compression visible in CH's Oct 2025 update) and Baltic-Continental synchronisation Nov 2025 (~8× step-change visible in KKME's S2 monthly trend chart). Same metric, different window + geography. See docs/methodology.md "Capacity reservation revenue" section for full reconciliation.

s3.interpretation: Cost stack within range. Lithium flat, cell prices tracking baseline. EU installed ~€164/kWh vs China €68/kWh gap persists.

2h.notes: 2h: PCS share higher per kWh. Grid scope drives most variance.

4h.notes: 4h: cell scale effects dominate. Energy block largest share.

grid_scope_classes.label: Light
grid_scope_classes.description: Existing HV bay. MV switchgear only.

cost_drivers.detail: LFP cell prices declining ~15% YoY. China overcapacity. Not fully passing through to EU turnkey.
Grid-forming requirements adding compliance cost. Supply adequate.
HV equipment lead times 10–16mo. Still the critical path for most projects. Prices elevated since 2021.
Euribor falling from 2023 peak. Improves LCOS and project IRR.

uncertainty.note: Grid scope is the single largest installed cost uncertainty in the Baltics.

trend.note: Equipment declining since 2023 peak. Grid + HV elevated.

lcos_reference.note: Reference range. Full computation in Revenue Engine.

technology.augmentation: Y8–12. 10–15% of original DC block cost.
technology.throughput_note: 1 cycle/day × 20yr × 4h ≈ 29 GWh/MW. Revenue potential and LCOS derive from this.
technology.notes: LFP dominant for utility-scale stationary. Sodium-ion emerging, unproven at grid scale.
technology.degradation_note: Slow early (Y1–5), linear mid-life (Y5–15), accelerates late. Calendar + cycling interact.

eu_turnkey_typical.label: EU turnkey typical
eu_turnkey_typical.note: Standard EPC, grid-heavy, mid-scale. This is the card's default range.

institutional_tso.label: Institutional / TSO
institutional_tso.note: Risk-heavy procurement, small scale, regulated overhead.

market_bands.note: No single 'true' CAPEX. Market is segmented by procurement capability, scale, and risk appetite.

lead_times.note: RTB to COD achievable in ~12 months if HV equipment ordered early. HV is the long pole, not battery.

scale_effect.note: Bulk procurement + shared grid scope drive savings at scale.

price_lag.note: Lithium ↓ today → turnkey battery ↓ in 3–6mo. HV equipment pricing lags 6–16mo.

supplier_spread.note: Premium buys bankability + warranty + delivery certainty.

contract_structure.note: Most Baltic projects use turnkey EPC. Split supply needs experienced developer.

policy_flags.detail: ENTSO-E Phase II Nov 2025. Grid-forming for new storage modules.

policy_flags.name: EU Batteries Regulation
policy_flags.detail: Sustainability, labelling, due diligence. Non-trivial documentation.

policy_flags.name: Baltic balancing cost shift
policy_flags.detail: 30% of balancing costs now on producers. Affects revenue, not CAPEX.
